subject: science
passage: Plants are usually thought of as silent. Yet when researchers placed microphones near tomato and tobacco plants, they recorded brief ultrasonic clicks, far too high-pitched for human ears, that became much more frequent when the plants were deprived of water or had their stems cut. Unstressed plants produced only occasional sounds. A computer program trained on the recordings could even distinguish a thirsty plant from a cut one. The clicks may result from air bubbles forming and bursting in the plant's water-conducting tissue, a purely physical process. Whether any insect or animal actually listens to them, and responds, has yet to be shown.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It reports a finding about stressed plants and then argues that insects use the sounds to locate weakened plants.
choices.B: It counters a common assumption with a finding, suggests a cause, and notes an open question.
choices.C: It describes a hypothesis about plants, explains how it was tested, and reports that the test failed to support it.
choices.D: It compares two plant species and then explains why one of them produces many more sounds than the other.

explanation.why: The text opens with a common belief ("Plants are usually thought of as silent"), counters it with the recordings, offers a possible cause ("The clicks may result from air bubbles"), and ends with an unanswered question about whether any animal "listens." The structure is assumption, contrary finding, possible explanation, open question.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says it "has yet to be shown" whether any animal listens, so it makes no such argument.
explanation.B: Correct. The text moves from "usually thought of as silent" to the recorded clicks, to the bubble explanation, to the unresolved question of listeners.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The recordings support the idea that plants make sounds; nothing in the text describes a failed test.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Tomato and tobacco are both studied, but the text compares stressed and unstressed plants, not the two species.
